decisions: The section is a diagnostic of the application snapshot after frameClock, not a name of the react-native root and not a JS API.
Counters are exact totals: the live roots plus the roots that ended, which add their counters when they are retired.
Phases are exclusive; RN's own layout telemetry is moved out of the JS turn the commit ran in, so the phases of a pump never add up to more than the pump.
Hermes' heap is read through jsi::Instrumentation::getHeapInfo, after a full collection only where the validation_collect_garbage_on_status meta is set.
The samples the percentiles come from are published only where the validation_performance_samples meta is set; the default snapshot carries aggregates.
Durations, the resident memory and Godot's static memory are recorded with provenance and never judged; the heap growth in the steady state is bounded at 2048 bytes.
The soak mounts and unmounts a root; the first render and the unmount commit run outside a pump, and the surfaces series time the retirement.
The leak sabotage is rejected by Godot's orphan count, not its node count: a Control that is removed and not freed is an orphan.
limitations: Local macOS arm64 evidence; hosted CI is pending and other targets are separate.
Headless only: no display, no GPU, no frame time of a presented frame; the headless loop paces its own frames (about 6.9 ms), so no duration here stands for a device.
No target-device budget is set (V2-D28) and no optimization is accepted or rejected by these numbers.
Text shaping (after GF-11), 10,000 rows (GF-15) and graphic frame time are not measured.
The mount and layout phases see only the commits that run inside a pump; React's first render and a root's unmount commit run outside one.
Percentiles are over the last 128 samples of a series; the total and the maximum are over its life.
The 2048-byte limit is a measurement of this host on this machine; a different Hermes, workload or runner needs it measured again.

Godot's static memory grows in steps that a plain Godot tree also shows (measured once by hand, not part of the harness) and the resident memory moves by tens of megabytes: both are recorded and cannot be limits.
This slice is the first of GF-30; it does not complete GF-30. Only GF-30's first-slice checkpoint (slice) closes: no whole GF, other checkpoint, weight or denominator closes.
